title: Owner waits and parallel slots
description: The output of `andon waiting --json`: what waits on the owner (a merge request, a decision, a task) and the parallel slots, counted only from what was decided for the current head. Written by the command to stdout and never kept. Read by the Chief of Staff (before launching an issue, and to order its questions) and by the owner's pane. The command alone holds the counting rule. Only these keys.

project.description: The project slug (the ledger's directory name).

slots.description: Parallel slots. Counts the doing and review issues of workers (not reviewer sub-issues, Chief Engineer issues or owner issues).

working.description: Counted issues that are not waiting on the owner.

waiting.description: Counted issues that have a merge or decision item.

free.description: 0 when waiting_full; otherwise limit minus working, never below 0.

waiting_full.description: true when waiting is limit or more: launch no new issue.

items.description: What waits on the owner. Calling items (call true) first, most held issues first, then oldest first; then the items left for later (call false), oldest first.

kind.description: merge: a pull request waiting on the owner's merge. decision: an open question of a decision kind not asked by the gate, or an owner issue that can start or is going with no question of a decision kind and no mark only_owner (no question, not answerable, a reason). An owner issue's decisions wait until every issue in its after is done; not_before does not hide them. task: an owner issue with the mark only_owner that can start or is going, with no question not yet received.

question.description: The question, <id>#<n>: the gate's question of a merge item, or the question of a decision item. Absent on the decision item of an owner issue with no question.

reason.description: Why it waits, for people. On a task item, the first line of only_owner; on the decision item of an owner issue with no question, what to fix.

ask.description: A copy of the question JSON (docs/contract.md section 5) of a decision item. Absent when the question has none.

answerable.description: Decision items only: whether the owner's pane may answer it (it has options and is not irreversible). false on an owner issue with no question.

steps.description: Task items only: the text of the issue's brief (issues/<id>/brief.md), trimmed, with line ends as LF; past 6000 characters it is cut and ends with a mark. What the owner does to finish the task. Absent when the brief is missing, not a regular file, unreadable, not UTF-8 or empty; past 1 MiB it is not read.

links.description: Task items only: the http(s) URLs in the whole brief, in order, each once. Absent when there are none.

items.description: A URL: http or https, printable ASCII.

holds.description: The issues not done that wait on this one through after, directly or behind those.

call.description: Whether the item calls the owner now (lights the lamp). false only when the item's issue can be left for later (an owner issue, or a todo or queued issue, whose mark later was last written by the Chief of Staff of that time with the current value), its later_until has not come, and every issue in holds can be left for later too. A merge item and the decision item of an owner issue with no question are always true. The command writes it on every item; it is not required so that inputs counted by an earlier version still pass (readers take an item without it by the old rule: merge and decision call, task does not).

later.description: The first line of the trusted mark later: why it can wait. Only on items (not merge) of an issue that can be left for later, whether call is true or false.

later_until.description: The issue's later_until, on items that have later and an issue with the key. From that day (in the ledger's timezone) the item calls again.

options.description: The options; the first is the recommendation.

pick.description: true only on the recommended option.

remaining.description: How many questions follow this one.
